message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles at this very moment. However, here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and you’ll see the current AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and you’ll get a live map, hourly updates, and a forecast. |
| **Weather Apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) display AQI for major cities. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Apps like AirVisual, Plume Labs’ Air Report, or the EPA’s own AirNow app give real‑time readings and alerts. |

### Quick Check (as of the last update I have)

- **Typical AQI range for LA**: 0–150 (Good to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups).  
- **Common pollutants**: PM₂.₅ (fine particulate matter), ozone (O₃), and sometimes PM₁₀.  
- **Health advice**: If the AQI is above 100, sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory conditions) should limit prolonged outdoor exertion.

If you’re looking for a historical trend or a forecast, the EPA’s AirNow site also offers a 7‑day outlook. For the absolute latest reading, just hit one of the links above or open your preferred weather app.
